title: Energy levels of screened charged impurity in gapped graphene under magnetic field
abstract: In this paper, we present a comprehensive theoretical study of the electronic states in gapped graphene in the presence of a charge impurity and a magnetic field. We focus on the impurity-induced modification of the Landau levels under the influence of an attractive or repulsive Coulomb potential. Since analytical solutions of the Dirac equation are not available in this case, the study is carried out using the Wentzel-Kramers-Brillouin (WKB) approach. Special attention is paid to the screening of the Coulomb potential in the presence of metallic gates situated at some distances from graphene sheet, as is commonly the case in experiments. Using both analytical and numerical methods, we determine the energy spectrum as a function of the magnetic field strength and impurity charge for screened and unscreened Coulomb potentials. Our results reveal a significant dependence of the energy levels for sample-to-gate distances of less than 50 nm.
summary: This paper provides a comprehensive theoretical analysis of how charged impurities perturb the Landau levels in gapped graphene under a magnetic field. By employing the WKB method, the authors specifically account for the screening of the Coulomb potential due to nearby metallic gates. The results highlight that the energy spectrum is strongly sensitive to the physical separation between the graphene and these gates.
main_problem: The study theoretically investigates the electronic energy levels of a charged impurity embedded in gapped graphene when subjected to a perpendicular magnetic field.
main_result: The energy spectrum shows a significant dependence on the screening distance of nearby metallic gates, which is a key feature distinguishing this work.
method: The Wentzel-Kramers-Brillouin (WKB) approximation is employed to solve the low-energy Dirac equation, supplemented by analytical and numerical techniques.
model_or_system: The system is gapped graphene, modeled by a Dirac Hamiltonian incorporating a screened Coulomb potential $V(r)$ from an impurity. The gap ($\Delta$) can be induced by substrates, and the potential is modified by screening from metallic gates.
key_observables: The energy spectrum, specifically the modified Landau levels, as a function of magnetic field strength and impurity charge.
important_parameters: Magnetic field strength ($B$), impurity charge ($Z$), gap parameter ($\Delta$), and the screening distance ($d$) to metallic gates.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is the applicability of the WKB method to the Dirac equation, which requires careful handling of the geometric phase. The potential is modeled as a screened Coulomb potential.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dependence of the distorted energy levels on the impurity charge ($g$) and the explicit dependence of these levels on the screening distance ($d$).
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first setting up the Hamiltonian and using WKB for the general case, then detailing the screened Coulomb potential model, and finally presenting numerical results showing the dependence of Landau levels on $Z$ and $B$.
why_interesting: The detailed analysis of how external environmental factors (like nearby gates) modify fundamental quantum states (Landau levels) in 2D Dirac materials is highly relevant to understanding engineered quantum devices.
